claims: Alabama Governor Kay Ivey signed SB57 into law as of April 2026.
SB57 restricts the purchase of candy, soda, and certain high-caffeine energy drinks over 65mg per 8oz using SNAP benefits.
The new restriction requires federal approval from the USDA.
The law targets a ban on candy, soda, and energy drinks containing stimulants like guarana or taurine.
Alabama SNAP benefits cannot be used for alcohol, tobacco, vitamins, medicine, hot prepared foods, pet food, or non-food household items.
Sports drinks aimed at hydration, such as Gatorade, are not included in the ban.
The new restrictions are not yet in effect.
The new restrictions require approval from the USDA Food and Nutrition Service.
For a family of three, SNAP gross income cannot exceed $2,694 per month.
$2,694 per month is 130% of the federal poverty level.
SNAP households must have assets such as cash or savings below $2,750.
